answer: For a poll on a cedar shelter after a gale, bidders submit escrowed bids for 100 ballots, each at least one ivory dollar. The server ranks funded bids, breaking ties by submission order, accepts the top 100 and charges each winner the lowest winning bid; it rejects and refunds the rest. Extra ballots require extra winning bids and cost at least one dollar each. Wealthy bidders can dominate; this prices ballots, not identities.
